detail:
The BrAIST trial (Weinstein et al., NEJM 2013) tested full-time bracing for adolescents with high-risk scoliosis curves. Bracing significantly decreased progression of high-risk curves to the surgical threshold. In the trial, 72% of braced patients reached skeletal maturity without their curve progressing to 50°, compared with 48% under observation. Wearing the brace more than about 13 hours per day was associated with a 90–93% success rate — compliance with wear hours was the biggest predictor of outcome. The trial was stopped early because of the efficacy shown.

This applies only during growth, until skeletal maturity is reached. Talk to your doctor if bracing is being considered.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
